title: Naming Conventions
text: myceliumr enforce specific sample ID formats, adopt consistent project-wide convention: WES Tumor: WES_T{subject} DNA_T{number} (e.g., “WES_T101”, “DNA_T001”) WES Normal: WES_N{subject} DNA_N{number} (e.g., “WES_N101”, “DNA_N001”) snRNA-seq: SN{subject}_{library} RNA_{subject}_{rep} (e.g., “SN101_1”, “RNA_T101_2”) Pair ID: {tumor_sample_id}__{normal_sample_id} (e.g., “WES_T101__WES_N101”, “DNA_T001__DNA_N001”)

title: Naming Conventions
text: Study objects: PascalCase, descriptive (e.g., my_study, nf1_study) explicitly named study examples. Cohort objects: PascalCase snake_case (e.g., cohort, nf1_cohort, study_cohort). Subject objects: Rarely used directly; accessed via cohort@subjects[[subject_id]]. AnalysisSpec objects: Use spec name primary identifier (stored registry name key). Data tables: snake_case _tbl suffix use descriptive names like subject_data, wes_samples.

title: Naming Conventions
code: # Study study <- study_new(   study_id = "NF1_001",   title = "NF1 Rat Genomics Study" )  # Cohort cohort <- cohort_new(   subject_tbl = subject_data,   sample_map = sample_data,   study = study )  # Access subject subject <- cohort@subjects[["RAT_101"]]  # Access analysis result <- cohort@analyses[["my_analysis_name"]]

title: Naming Conventions
text: Constructor functions: {noun}_new() (e.g., study_new(), cohort_new()) Validation functions: validate_{noun}() (e.g., validate_manifest(), validate_cohort()) Accessor/getter functions: get_{property}() simply reference property directly (e.g., cohort@subject_tbl) IO functions: read_{format}() write_{format}() (e.g., read_manifest_csv()) Helper functions: lowercase underscores (e.g., extract_pair_ids()) S7 methods: Dispatch class; function name describes operation (e.g., print() method Cohort)

title: Naming Conventions
text: Class definitions: classes.R Constructors: constructors.R Validation: validate.R, validate_manifest.R IO (read/write): io.R Methods utilities: {feature}.R (e.g., analysis_registry.R, print.R)

title: Naming Conventions
text: Raw data: Use consistent prefix descriptor (e.g., manifest_nf1_001.csv, cohort_pilot_data.rda) Intermediate data: {description}_{date}.rda {description}_{version}.fst Results: {analysis}_{date}_{version}.csv {analysis}_results.rda

title: Naming Conventions
text: Input data: Describe clearly (e.g., meta_rats, subject_tbl, sample_map) Flags: Prefix is_ has_ (e.g., is_valid, has_missing) Counts: Prefix n_ (e.g., n_subjects, n_samples) Logical conditions: strict, verbose, allow_* (e.g., allow_rna_duplicates)

title: Naming Conventions
text: Output vectors/lists: Descriptive plural singular depending context Named lists: Keys identifiers logical names (e.g., cohort@subjects[["RAT_101"]])

title: Naming Conventions

title: S7 AnalysisSpec class — AnalysisSpec
text: immutable S7 class defining analysis specifications Cohort. AnalysisSpec objects describe locate, read, interpret analysis output files templated paths standardized readers.

title: S7 AnalysisSpec class — AnalysisSpec
code: AnalysisSpec(   name = character(0),   assay = character(0),   level = character(0),   format = character(0),   description = NA_character_,   path_template = NA_character_,   root_key = NA_character_,   reader = character(0),   key_cols = character(0) )

title: S7 AnalysisSpec class — AnalysisSpec
text: name Character scalar unique analysis name (key registry). assay Character scalar assay type (e.g., "wes_somatic", "wes_germline", "snrna"). Required. level Character scalar data organization level. Must one : "subject", "pair", "cohort". Required. format Character scalar file format (e.g., "rds", "tsv", "txt"). Required. description Character scalar human-readable description analysis. Optional, defaults NA. path_template Character scalar templated path analysis output. Supports substitution tokens: {root}, {subject_id}, {tumor_id}, {normal_id}, {pair_id}. Optional, defaults NA. root_key Character scalar key cohort@paths list use {root} template value (e.g., "msi_root", "sig_root", "wes_root"). Optional, defaults NA. reader Character scalar function name read files matching spec (e.g., "read_msi_txt", "read.csv"). Must valid function name. Required. key_cols Character vector column names use keys loading analysis table. Determines rows indexed (e.g., c("subject_id") c("pair_id")). Required.

title: S7 AnalysisSpec class — AnalysisSpec
text: Use analysis_spec_new() construct AnalysisSpec objects immediate validation. AnalysisSpec objects typically registered Cohort via analysis_register(). Access properties via @ operator:
code: spec@name spec@assay spec@level spec@format spec@description spec@path_template spec@root_key spec@reader spec@key_cols

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: immutable S7 class managing cross-species cohort data. Cohorts combine validated subject-level metadata sample--assay mappings optional study context, file paths, analysis results. primary data container WES snRNA-seq analyses across rat, mouse, human studies.

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
code: Cohort(   study = NULL,   subjects = list(),   subject_tbl = NULL,   sample_map = NULL,   paths = list(),   analyses = list(),   registry = list(),   cache = list() )

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: study Study object providing project-level context metadata, NULL applicable. Optional. subjects Named list Subject objects, automatically created subject_tbl rows cohort construction. Names subject IDs. Access individual subjects via: cohort@subjects[["RAT001"]]. subject_tbl tibble (data frame) containing subject-level metadata. Required columns: subject_id (character), species (rat/mouse/human). Optional columns: sex, strain, genotype, cohort, timepoint, notes. Validated validate_cohort(). sample_map tibble mapping subjects assay-specific sample IDs. Must include subject_id column referential integrity. Additional columns typically include assay_wes_id, assay_snrna_id, etc. Validated validate_cohort(). paths Named list file paths data files results directories. Optional, defaults empty list. analyses Named list containing analysis results, intermediate tables, data objects later retrieval. Optional, defaults empty list. registry Named list AnalysisSpec objects defining registered analyses. Names correspond spec@name. Optional, defaults empty list. cache Named list optional memoization loaded analysis data. Optional, defaults empty list.

title: S7 Cohort class — Cohort
text: Use cohort_new() construct Cohort objects comprehensive validation. Validation ensures: Required columns subject_tbl sample_map Valid species values (rat/mouse/human) Referential integrity subject_tbl sample_map duplicate subject IDs Access properties via @ operator:
code: cohort@study         # Study object or NULL cohort@subjects      # Named list of Subject objects cohort@subjects[["RAT001"]]  # Individual Subject object cohort@subject_tbl   # Subject metadata table (for bulk operations) cohort@sample_map    # Sample mapping table cohort@paths         # File paths cohort@analyses      # Stored analysis results cohort@registry      # Named list of AnalysisSpec objects cohort@cache         # Memoization cache

title: S7 Study class — Study
text: immutable S7 class storing research project metadata cross-species genomics studies. Study objects provide high-level context configuration cohorts analyses involving rat, mouse, human subjects.

title: S7 Study class — Study
code: Study(   study_id = character(0),   title = character(0),   description = NA_character_,   hypotheses = character(0),   aims = character(0),   assays = character(0),   genome_builds = list(),   created_at = NULL,   tags = character(0) )

title: S7 Study class — Study
text: study_id Character scalar study identifier. Unique within project. title Character scalar study name/title. description Character scalar longer description study purpose, design, protocols. Can file path (ending .md, .txt, .rtf) read README content. Optional. hypotheses Character vector research hypotheses. Accepts multiple hypotheses. Optional. aims Character vector specific research aims. Accepts multiple aims. Optional. assays Character vector assay types used (e.g., "WES", "snRNA-seq"). Optional. genome_builds Named list mapping species genome build versions (e.g., list(rat = "rn7", mouse = "mm10", human = "hg38")). Supports rn6, rn7 rat; mm9, mm10, mm39 mouse; hg19, hg38 human. Optional. created_at POSIXct timestamp creation. Defaults current time. tags Character vector arbitrary tags categorization. Optional.

title: S7 Study class — Study
text: Use study_new() construct Study objects immediate validation. Access properties via @ operator:
code: study@study_id study@title study@description study@hypotheses study@aims study@assays study@genome_builds study@created_at study@tags

title: S7 Subject class — Subject

title: S7 Subject class — Subject
code: Subject(   subject_id = character(0),   species = character(0),   sex = NA_character_,   strain = NA_character_,   genotype = NA_character_,   cohort = NA_character_,   timepoint = NA_character_,   notes = NA_character_ )

title: S7 Subject class — Subject
text: subject_id Character scalar unique subject identifier. species Character scalar species designation. Must one : "rat", "mouse", "human" (validated subject_new()). sex Character scalar biological sex (e.g., "M", "F"). Optional. strain Character scalar strain breed designation. Optional. genotype Character scalar genetic background modification (e.g., "WT", "KO"). Optional. cohort Character scalar cohort membership treatment group. Optional. timepoint Character scalar study timepoint collection date. Optional. notes Character scalar free-form annotations. Optional.

code: # Create and register specs study <- study_new(study_id = "STUDY001", title = "My Study") manifest <- data.frame(   rat_id = c(101, 102),   wes_tumor_id = c("WES_T1", "WES_T2"),   wes_normal_id = c("WES_N1", "WES_N2"),   sn_id = I(list("RNA_T1", "RNA_T2")) ) parsed <- validate_manifest(manifest) cohort <- cohort_new(   subject_tbl = parsed$subject_tbl,   sample_map = parsed$sample_map,   study = study )  spec1 <- analysis_spec_new(   name = "somatic_vars",   assay = "wes_somatic",   level = "pair",   format = "tsv",   reader = "read_tsv",   key_cols = c("pair_id") )  spec2 <- analysis_spec_new(   name = "gene_expr",   assay = "snrna",   level = "subject",   format = "rds",   reader = "readRDS",   key_cols = c("subject_id") )  cohort <- analysis_register(cohort, spec1) cohort <- analysis_register(cohort, spec2) analysis_list(cohort) #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   name         assay       level   format reader   root_key #>   <chr>        <chr>       <chr>   <chr>  <chr>    <chr>    #> 1 somatic_vars wes_somatic pair    tsv    read_tsv NA       #> 2 gene_expr    snrna       subject rds    readRDS  NA

Access individual Subject objects (automatically created) rat_subject <- cohort@subjects[["101"]] print(rat_subject) #> <myceliumr::Subject> #>  @ subject_id: chr "101" #>  @ species   : chr "rat" #>  @ sex       : chr "M" #>  @ strain    : chr NA #>  @ genotype  : chr NA #>  @ cohort    : chr NA #>  @ timepoint : chr NA #>  @ notes     : chr NA

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
text: Reads CSV file containing cross-species subject metadata, DNA sample identifiers, optional RNA sample identifiers. Validates structures data subject-level, WES pair-level, RNA-level, sample mapping tables suitable creating Cohort object.

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
code: read_manifest_csv(path, ..., allow_rna_duplicates = FALSE)

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
text: path Character scalar file path CSV manifest file. Path must exist file must readable. ... Additional named arguments passed readr::read_csv(), col_types, skip, comment, etc. allow_rna_duplicates Logical. TRUE, allows rna_sample_id appear multiple times subject_id. FALSE (default), errors duplicates. Default: FALSE.

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
text: list four elements: subject_tbl: Tibble one row per subject_id wes_pair_tbl: Tibble one row per subject_id (includes DNA/WES IDs) rna_tbl: Tibble zero rows per subject_id sample_map: Long-format tibble columns: subject_id, assay, sample_id, role

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
text: subject must exactly one DNA tumor sample one DNA normal sample. subject can zero RNA tumor samples. manifest can multiple rows per subject differ rna_sample_id. manifest CSV must contain required columns: subject_id: Unique identifier subject (character) species: Species designation - one "rat", "mouse", "human" (character) dna_tumor_id: DNA tumor sample identifier (character) dna_normal_id: DNA normal sample identifier (character) wes_tumor_sample_id: WES tumor sample identifier (character) wes_normal_sample_id: WES normal sample identifier (character) Optional subject metadata columns: sex: Biological sex strain: Strain breed designation genotype: Genetic background modification cohort: Treatment group cohort membership timepoint: Study timepoint collection date notes: Free-form annotations Optional sample column: rna_sample_id: RNA tumor sample identifier (can repeat per subject)

title: Read and validate a manifest CSV file — read_manifest_csv
code: # Create a temporary CSV manifest manifest_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv") header <- paste0(   "subject_id,species,dna_tumor_id,dna_normal_id,",   "wes_tumor_sample_id,wes_normal_sample_id,rna_sample_id" ) writeLines(   c(     header,     "RAT001,rat,DNA_T1,DNA_N1,WES_T1,WES_N1,RNA_T1",     "RAT001,rat,DNA_T1,DNA_N1,WES_T1,WES_N1,RNA_T2",     "RAT002,rat,DNA_T2,DNA_N2,WES_T2,WES_N2,"   ),   manifest_file )  # Read and validate the manifest manifest_split <- read_manifest_csv(manifest_file) print(manifest_split$subject_tbl) #> # A tibble: 2 × 2 #>   subject_id species #>   <chr>      <chr>   #> 1 RAT001     rat     #> 2 RAT002     rat     print(manifest_split$wes_pair_tbl) #> # A tibble: 2 × 6 #>   subject_id dna_tumor_id dna_normal_id wes_tumor_sample_id wes_normal_sample_id #>   <chr>      <chr>        <chr>         <chr>               <chr>                #> 1 RAT001     DNA_T1       DNA_N1        WES_T1              WES_N1               #> 2 RAT002     DNA_T2       DNA_N2        WES_T2              WES_N2               #> # ℹ 1 more variable: pair_id <chr> print(manifest_split$rna_tbl) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   subject_id assay     tumor_sample_id #>   <chr>      <chr>     <chr>           #> 1 RAT001     rna_snrna RNA_T1          #> 2 RAT001     rna_snrna RNA_T2          print(manifest_split$sample_map) #> # A tibble: 6 × 4 #>   subject_id assay     sample_id role   #>   <chr>      <chr>     <chr>     <chr>  #> 1 RAT001     dna_wes   WES_T1    tumor  #> 2 RAT002     dna_wes   WES_T2    tumor  #> 3 RAT001     dna_wes   WES_N1    normal #> 4 RAT002     dna_wes   WES_N2    normal #> 5 RAT001     rna_snrna RNA_T1    tumor  #> 6 RAT001     rna_snrna RNA_T2    tumor

title: Create a Study object — study_new
text: Constructs Study object describe overall research project, including study metadata, research hypotheses aims, assay types, genome build information. Studies serve container cohorts provide context cross-species genomics analysis.

title: Create a Study object — study_new
code: study_new(   study_id,   title,   description = NA_character_,   hypotheses = character(),   aims = character(),   assays = character(),   genome_builds = list(),   created_at = Sys.time(),   tags = character() )

title: Create a Study object — study_new
text: study_id Character scalar providing unique identifier study. Must least 1 character long. title Character scalar study name/title. Must least 1 character long. description Character scalar optional longer description study purpose design. Can file path (ending .md, .txt, .rtf) read description field. Defaults NA. hypotheses Character vector research hypotheses. Accepts multiple hypotheses. Optional defaults empty vector. aims Character vector specific research aims. Accepts multiple aims. Optional defaults empty vector. assays Character vector assay types used study (e.g., "WES", "snRNA-seq"). Optional defaults empty vector. genome_builds Named list mapping species names genome build versions (e.g., list(rat = "rn7", mouse = "mm10")). Supports rn6, rn7 rat; mm9, mm10, mm39 mouse; hg19, hg38 human. Optional defaults empty list. created_at POSIXct timestamp study creation. Defaults current time. tags Character vector arbitrary tags categorization. Optional defaults empty vector.

title: Create a Study object — study_new
text: Study object containing provided metadata.

title: Create a Study object — study_new
text: Study objects S7 classes immutably store research project metadata. provide context cohorts support cross-species genomics analysis. study_id title required; fields optional. description parameter accepts either plain text file path. file path ending .md, .txt, .rtf provided, file contents read stored description field. allows storing detailed README content within study metadata.

code: # Example with multiple hypotheses and aims study <- study_new(   study_id = "STUDY001",   title = "Cross-species genomics comparison",   description = "Comparing rat and mouse genomes",   hypotheses = c(     "Orthologous genes show conserved expression patterns",     "Disease genes are enriched in specific pathways"   ),   aims = c(     "Map regulatory regions across species",     "Identify conserved non-coding elements"   ),   assays = c("WES", "snRNA-seq"),   genome_builds = list(rat = "rn7", mouse = "mm10", human = "hg38") ) print(study) #> <myceliumr::Study> #>  @ study_id     : chr "STUDY001" #>  @ title        : chr "Cross-species genomics comparison" #>  @ description  : chr "Comparing rat and mouse genomes" #>  @ hypotheses   : chr [1:2] "Orthologous genes show conserved expression patterns" ... #>  @ aims         : chr [1:2] "Map regulatory regions across species" ... #>  @ assays       : chr [1:2] "WES" "snRNA-seq" #>  @ genome_builds:List of 3 #>  .. $ rat  : chr "rn7" #>  .. $ mouse: chr "mm10" #>  .. $ human: chr "hg38" #>  @ created_at   : POSIXct[1:1], format: "2026-02-05 07:59:44" #>  @ tags         : chr(0)   # Example with README file as description # study <- study_new( #   study_id = "STUDY002", #   title = "My Study", #   description = "path/to/README.md" # )

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: Ensures Cohort object satisfies structural integrity requirements cross-species genomics analysis. Validates subject table, sample map, referential integrity . Intended internal validation step called automatically cohort_new().

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
code: validate_cohort(x)

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: x S7 object expected Cohort class instance.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: Invisibly returns TRUE validation succeeds. Throws informative errors validation fails.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
text: VALIDATION CHECKS: x actually Cohort object subject_tbl sample_map data frames subject_tbl includes required columns: subject_id, species sample_map includes subject_id column subject_id species character vectors, non-empty duplicate subject_id values subject_tbl species values valid (rat/mouse/human) Referential integrity: sample_map$subject_id values exist subject_tbl Validation performed automatically cohort_new(), can called directly debugging custom Cohort construction.

title: Validate a Cohort object — validate_cohort
code: # Create valid cohort components subjects <- data.frame(   subject_id = "RAT001",   species = "rat",   sex = "M" ) samples <- data.frame(   subject_id = "RAT001",   assay_wes_id = "WES_R001" ) cohort <- cohort_new(   subject_tbl = subjects,   sample_map = samples )  # Validation succeeds (called automatically above) validate_cohort(cohort)

what: Validate and structure a manifest for cross-species genomics study — validate_manifest
title: Validate and structure a manifest for cross-species genomics study — validate_manifest
text: Validates structures metadata rat (species) genomic studies standardized subject-level sample-level tables. Handles WES (DNA) snRNA-seq (RNA) assays flexible support missing data.

title: Validate and structure a manifest for cross-species genomics study — validate_manifest
code: validate_manifest(   meta_rats,   meta_samples = NULL,   strict = FALSE,   allow_rna_duplicates = FALSE )

title: Validate and structure a manifest for cross-species genomics study — validate_manifest
text: meta_rats data.frame one row per rat/subject containing metadata sample identifiers. Required columns: rat_id (numeric). Optional columns: rat_genotype, cohort, has_wes (logical), has_snrna (logical), wes_tumor_id, wes_normal_id (character), sn_id (list character vectors), species (character; defaults "rat" missing), plus additional metadata columns (age, sex, strain, timepoint, etc.). meta_samples Optional data.frame multiple rows per rat, typically sample-level metadata. Expected columns: sample_id (chr), sample_type (chr), lw_id (chr, optional), rat_id (numeric), sample_phenotype (chr: "tumor"/"normal"), plus optional QC columns. NA/NULL, sample_tbl returned. strict Logical. TRUE, requires rat DNA tumor DNA normal sample IDs. FALSE (default), missing DNA RNA samples allowed. Default: FALSE. allow_rna_duplicates Logical. TRUE, allows duplicate RNA sample IDs within rat_id. FALSE (default), duplicates trigger error.

title: Validate and structure a manifest for cross-species genomics study — validate_manifest
text: list elements: subject_tbl: Tibble one row per rat_id (meta_rats species added). dna_tbl: Tibble one row per rat_id containing assay identifiers DNA (WES) samples. Columns: rat_id, assay, tumor_sample_id, normal_sample_id, pair_id. rna_tbl: Tibble 0..N rows per rat_id. Columns: rat_id, assay, tumor_sample_id (RNA sample identifier). sample_map: Long-format tibble mapping rats samples. Columns: rat_id, assay, sample_id, role. completeness_tbl: Tibble one row per rat_id summarizing data availability. Columns: rat_id, has_dna_tumor, has_dna_normal, has_dna_pair, n_rna_samples. sample_tbl (optional): meta_samples provided, tibble standardized sample metadata. Columns: sample_id, rat_id, assay, role, lw_id.

title: Validate and structure a manifest for cross-species genomics study — validate_manifest
text: BEHAVIOR: Empty strings wes_tumor_id, wes_normal_id treated missing. sn_id column meta_rats list element : NA NULL (interpreted RNA samples rat) character vector 0 RNA sample IDs pair_id computed tumor_sample_id normal_sample_id non-missing non-empty: paste0(tumor, "__", normal). Strict mode enforces DNA tumor DNA normal present every rat; missing, throws validation error. RNA sample duplicates within rat_id trigger error unless allow_rna_duplicates = TRUE.

title: Validate and structure a manifest for cross-species genomics study — validate_manifest
code: # Create sample data meta_rats <- data.frame(   rat_id = c(101, 102, 103),   rat_genotype = c("WT", "NF1+/-", "WT"),   cohort = c("A", "A", "B"),   wes_tumor_id = c("T1", "T2", NA),   wes_normal_id = c("N1", "N2", NA),   sn_id = I(list(     c("RNA_T1_1", "RNA_T1_2"),     c("RNA_T2_1"),     NA_character_   )) )  result <- validate_manifest(meta_rats) print(result$subject_tbl) #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>   subject_id rat_genotype cohort species #>   <chr>      <chr>        <chr>  <chr>   #> 1 101        WT           A      rat     #> 2 102        NF1+/-       A      rat     #> 3 103        WT           B      rat     print(result$dna_tbl) #> # A tibble: 3 × 5 #>   subject_id assay   tumor_sample_id normal_sample_id pair_id #>   <chr>      <chr>   <chr>           <chr>            <chr>   #> 1 101        dna_wes T1              N1               T1__N1  #> 2 102        dna_wes T2              N2               T2__N2  #> 3 103        dna_wes NA              NA               NA      print(result$rna_tbl) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   subject_id assay     tumor_sample_id #>   <chr>      <chr>     <chr>           #> 1 101        rna_snrna RNA_T1_1        #> 2 101        rna_snrna RNA_T1_2        #> 3 102        rna_snrna RNA_T2_1
